engines.source: Aerojet Rocketdyne RL10 datasheet (RL10B-2: 465.5 s vac, 24,750 lbf); upper-stage engine
engines.note: Highest chemical Isp, but LH2 boils off (20 K storage) within days-weeks, so cryogenic propulsion is used on upper stages, not on long-lived satellites; thrust is also orders of magnitude above what a cm/s avoidance burn can be metered with.

engines.source: Aerojet Rocketdyne R-4D datasheet (R-4D-11: 490 N, ~312 s); GEO apogee engines / Orion ESM aux
engines.note: Storable hypergolic biprop: high thrust, years-long storage; typical on GEO buses and large LEO platforms.

engines.source: Aerojet Rocketdyne Advanced Material Bipropellant Rocket (AMBR) datasheet, ~333 s / 623 N
engines.note: Iridium-rhenium chamber dual-mode biprop: best storable chemical Isp in this list.

engines.source: Aerojet Rocketdyne MR-106L 22 N datasheet (Isp ~228-235 s)
engines.note: Workhorse catalytic hydrazine thruster for orbit maintenance and avoidance; toxic propellant.

engines.source: Aerojet Rocketdyne MR-103G 1 N datasheet (Isp 202-224 s over blowdown)
engines.note: Small 1 N hydrazine thruster used for attitude/fine Δv; fine impulse resolution for cm/s burns.

engines.source: Bradford ECAPS 1N HPGP datasheet (Isp 204-235 s); flown on PRISMA (2010), SkySat
engines.note: Low-toxicity ADN monoprop; ~6 % higher Isp and ~24 % higher density-Isp than hydrazine.

engines.source: NASA Green Propellant Infusion Mission (GPIM, 2019) GR-1 thruster, ~231 s
engines.note: HAN-based green monoprop flight-proven on GPIM; needs catalyst-bed preheat before firing.

engines.source: Sutton & Biblarz, Rocket Propulsion Elements (N2 cold gas Isp ~60-73 s); e.g. Moog 58-series valves
engines.note: Simplest, cleanest system (no combustion); very low Isp so large Δv costs a lot of gas.

engines.source: OKB Fakel SPT-100 datasheet (83 mN, ~1600 s at 1.35 kW); >100 GEO satellites
engines.note: Hall thruster: ~7x less propellant than hydrazine but tens of mN, so avoidance needs long arcs planned ahead.

engines.source: Busek BHT-600 datasheet (39 mN, ~1530 s at 600 W)
engines.note: Small-sat Hall thruster (constellation class, cf. Starlink/OneWeb Hall propulsion).

engines.source: NASA NSTAR ion engine (Deep Space 1, Dawn): 92 mN, 3100 s at 2.3 kW
engines.note: Gridded ion: highest Isp, lowest propellant, but burn times of hours for m/s-class Δv.

engines.source: QinetiQ T6 gridded ion thruster (BepiColombo): 145 mN, ~4120 s at 4.5 kW
engines.note: Kaufman gridded ion engine: very high Isp; power-hungry (kW class).
